members: Diazepam - long t½ (20-100h), active metabolite desmethyldiazepam (Dulcan p.687, DSM p.629)
Lorazepam - intermediate t½ (10-20h), Phase II glucuronidation, preferred in liver disease & catatonia (Dulcan p.153, p.1023)
Alprazolam - short t½ (12-15h), fast onset, high rebound/addiction risk, avoid in youth (Dulcan p.264, DSM p.624)
Midazolam - ultra-short t½ (1.5-3h), intranasal (IN) procedural sedation (Dulcan p.100)
Clonazepam - long t½ (30-40h), no active metabolites, sustained anxiolysis (Dulcan p.484)
Buspirone - non-BZD 5-HT1A partial agonist, slow onset (2-4w), no dependence (DSM p.621, StahlNeuro p.369)
drug_class.mechanism: BZD = GABA_A positive allosteric modulators (PAMs) increasing Cl- channel opening frequency (StahlNeuro p.260); Buspirone = 5-HT1A partial agonist with presynaptic autoreceptor desensitization (StahlNeuro p.369)
kinetics: Phase I CYP3A4/CYP2C19 oxidation (Diazepam, Alprazolam, Midazolam) (Dulcan p.687)
Phase II direct glucuronidation (Lorazepam - LOT) safe in hepatic impairment (Dulcan p.153)
Higher free fraction and faster hepatic clearance in prepubertal children (StahlKids p.182)
drug_class.onset_of_effect: BZD = immediate (minutes to hours); Buspirone = delayed (2-4 weeks)

items: Acute severe anxiety, panic attacks, and agitation PRN (Dulcan p.264, p.612)
Pediatric catatonia treatment and diagnostic challenge (Lorazepam) (Dulcan p.1023)
Intranasal procedural sedation in children (Midazolam) (Dulcan p.100)
Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) chronic treatment (Buspirone) (Dulcan p.333)
Self-injurious behaviors (SIBs) and agitation in ASD/IDD (Buspirone) (Dulcan p.333, StahlKids p.51)
key_numbers: 1-2 mg - Lorazepam IV/PO dose for Catatonia Challenge (Dulcan p.1023)
0.2-0.3 mg/kg - Midazolam IN dose for procedural sedation (Dulcan p.100)
2-4 weeks - Onset time for Buspirone therapeutic effect (StahlNeuro p.369)
5 mg BID - Starting pediatric dose for Buspirone (StahlKids p.51)

items: Sedation, drowsiness, and ataxia via alpha1 GABA_A subunit (StahlNeuro p.260)
Anterograde amnesia and cognitive impairment (StahlNeuro p.260, p.422)
Paradoxical reactions (disinhibition, aggression, hyperactivity) in young children/ASD/ADHD (Dulcan p.687)
Withdrawal seizures and delirium upon abrupt cessation (DSM p.624, p.629)

key_numbers: alpha1 - GABA_A subunit mediating sedation, amnesia, and tolerance (StahlNeuro p.260)
alpha2/alpha3 - GABA_A subunits mediating anxiolysis and muscle relaxation (StahlNeuro p.260)
0.4% - Baseline seizure risk threshold in psychotropic safety contexts (Dulcan p.718)

items: Assess baseline anxiety severity, substance use history, and liver function (Dulcan p.153, p.264)
Monitor for excessive sedation, cognitive slowing, and academic impact (StahlKids p.314)
Watch for paradoxical disinhibition or behavioral escalation in young children (Dulcan p.687)
Follow strict tapering protocol of 10%-25% dose reduction every 1-2 weeks (Dulcan p.688)
Monitor BP during alpha2-agonist or complex anxiolytic combination therapy (Dulcan p.612)
key_numbers: 10%-25% - Weekly/biweekly dose reduction percentage during BZD taper (Dulcan p.688)
1-2 weeks - Minimum interval between BZD dose reduction steps (Dulcan p.688)

items: Start Low, Go Slow titration rule in pediatric prescribing (StahlKids p.33)
Avoid Alprazolam in children and adolescents due to addiction/diversion risk (Dulcan p.264)
Use Lorazepam for liver disease patients as it bypasses Phase I CYP metabolism (Dulcan p.153)
Educate families that Buspirone requires daily adherence and lacks PRN effect (StahlKids p.51)
Use intranasal atomizer device for rapid Midazolam administration in emergency/ED (Dulcan p.100)
key_numbers: 15-30 mg/day - Target therapeutic dose range for Buspirone in youth (StahlKids p.51)
30-60 minutes - Response evaluation window after Lorazepam Catatonia Challenge (Dulcan p.1023)

high_yield: BZD increases GABA_A Cl- channel opening frequency (PAM), while barbiturates increase duration (StahlNeuro p.260, Syllabus p.50)
Lorazepam is the preferred BZD in liver failure and for Catatonia Challenge (1-2 mg) (Dulcan p.153, p.1023)
Avoid Alprazolam in youth due to rapid onset, short t½, inter-dose rebound, and diversion risk (Dulcan p.264, DSM p.624)
Flumazenil administration to chronic BZD users can precipitate life-threatening seizures (StahlNeuro p.614, DSM p.625)
Buspirone is a 5-HT1A partial agonist with slow onset (2-4w), zero addiction/abuse potential, effective for GAD & SIBs in ASD/IDD (DSM p.621, StahlNeuro p.369, Dulcan p.333)
